assets.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. A consistent 2D game walking sprite sheet. Image 1 is the reference character, image 2 is her approved walk and style, and image 3 is a 16-frame pose and CAMERA guide. Redraw each cell of Image 3 in the visual style of image 2. Camera: low viewpoint, looking upward from below the person, three-quarter horizontal angle, preserve image 3's exact foreshortening and perspective, do not replace with an eye-level view. Preserve each cell's arms and foot poses, row-major timing and position. Same faceless adult woman with shoulder-length dark hair, soft grey short-sleeved top, dark full-length trousers and pale sneakers. Clean smooth clothing edges and clearly separated limbs, same grayscale palette as image 2. Exactly sixteen full-body figures in an evenly spaced 4 by 4 grid, transparent background, empty margins around each complete figure; no labels, dividers, objects or facial features.

Use case: style-transfer. Image 1 is the edit target: a transparent 4 by 4 sprite sheet of the SAME woman seen from a camera high above looking DOWN at 55 degrees. Redraw each of its sixteen figures in place, keeping image 1's EXACT overhead camera, foreshortened body proportions, pose, positions and grid. At this steep downward angle show mostly the crown of her hair, shoulders above her feet, and foreshortened legs exactly as in the target. Image 2 is only the grayscale visual style and clothing reference. Dress this same faceless adult woman in the grey short-sleeved top, dark long trousers and pale sneakers, with dark shoulder-length hair. Clean smooth boundaries, no facial features. Keep sixteen original distinct walking poses, cell-by-cell, no added graphics or text, transparent background. Preserve the steep high viewing angle; do not rotate or straighten the figure to face the viewer.

Use case: style-transfer. Image 1 is the exact established 16-frame walking animation and appearance for a faceless woman. Image 2 contains 16 intermediate poses, each falling halfway between the matching numbered frame in Image 1 and its next frame. Create a matching 4 by 4 transparent sprite sheet of those intermediate poses. For every cell follow Image 2's position of feet and arms, but use Image 1's matching character design, face, hair shape, clothing, grey values, shoes, perspective and rendering style. Do not change the scale, body position, framing, camera or background between cells or relative to image 1. Match the very same woman in a grey short-sleeved top, long dark trousers and pale sneakers. The purpose is smooth animation when these drawings alternate between Image 1's frames; each must look like a subtle halfway step, never a different character or outfit. Exactly 16 complete isolated frames, smooth uncluttered edges, no text or props.
